pipes.d.type: Open at both ends, or closed at one (the right) end
pipes.d.nOpen: Harmonic number of the open pipe, $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$ (resonant frequency $f_n = nv/2L$)
pipes.d.nClosed: Harmonic number of the closed pipe, odd only, $n = 1, 3, 5, \dots$ (resonant frequency $f_n = nv/4L$)
pipes.d.L: Length $L$ of the pipe; the standing-wave pattern stays the same and the frequency scales as $1/L$
pipes.d.sound: Play a pure tone at the current resonant frequency $f_n$ (mind the volume)
pipes.goal.ends: End conditions: an open end is a displacement antinode ($\mathrm{A}_s$) and a pressure node ($\mathrm{N}_p$); a closed end is a displacement node ($\mathrm{N}_s$) and a pressure antinode ($\mathrm{A}_p$). Since $\Delta p = -B\,\partial s/\partial x$, displacement nodes and pressure antinodes coincide
pipes.goal.harm: Only wavelengths that fit both ends resonate: open pipe $\lambda = 2L/n$, $f_n = nv/2L$ (every $n$); closed pipe $\lambda = 4L/n$, $f_n = nv/4L$ (odd $n$ only)
pipes.obs.open1: Default (open pipe, $L$ = 1.00 m, $n$ = 1): displacement antinodes at both ends and one displacement node in the middle. $\lambda = 2L$ = 2.00 m, $f_1$ = 172 Hz
pipes.obs.dots: The air particles (columns of dots) oscillate along the pipe. Blue columns sit at the displacement nodes and antinodes: a column at a node (on a dotted line) stays put, a column at an antinode moves the most
pipes.obs.density: Why the density changes at a node: at a displacement node ($\mathrm{N}_s$) the air does not move, but the columns on both sides close in and spread out, so the density (pressure) changes most there, a pressure antinode ($\mathrm{A}_p$). At a displacement antinode ($\mathrm{A}_s$) the air moves most, but its neighbours move the same way by the same amount, so the spacing stays: no density change, a pressure node ($\mathrm{N}_p$)
pipes.obs.np: N = node, A = antinode. Subscript and colour tell the graphs apart: $\mathrm{N}_s$, $\mathrm{A}_s$ for the displacement $s$ (blue), $\mathrm{N}_p$, $\mathrm{A}_p$ for the pressure $\Delta p$ (pink). Dotted vertical lines = displacement nodes = pressure antinodes. Neighbouring nodes are $\lambda/2$ apart
pipes.obs.closed: Closed pipe: the particles at the closed end do not move (displacement node). Only $n$ = 1, 3, 5, … exist; for the same $L$, $f_1$ = 85.8 Hz, half that of the open pipe
pipes.obs.L: Doubling the length halves every resonant frequency ($f_n \propto 1/L$)
pipes.obs.sound: With sound on, step $n$ up through the harmonics: the open pipe gives every integer multiple of $f_1$, the closed pipe only the odd multiples
pipes.assume.v: Speed of sound in air $v$ = 343 m/s (20 °C)
pipes.assume.end: An open end is exactly a displacement antinode (no end correction); rigid, lossless walls. The right end is the closed one
pipes.assume.graph: The displacement graph plots the displacement $s$ along the pipe (horizontal, right +) vertically. The lower graph is both the pressure change and the density change: $\Delta\rho/\rho = -\partial s/\partial x = \Delta p/B$. Pink shading in the pipe = compression ($\Delta p > 0$), white = rarefaction
pipes.assume.slow: The animation runs at one cycle every 2 s whatever the real frequency; particle displacements and graph heights are magnified (real amplitudes are of the order of micrometres)
